distractors.reason: 'Good' is an adjective. After a verb we need an adverb, so we say 'sleep well', not 'sleep good'.
We don't say 'sleep fast'. 'Fast' describes speed, like 'run fast' or 'eat fast'.
We don't say 'sleep hard' with this meaning. 'Hard' means 'with great effort', as in 'work hard'.

example_sentence: I always sleep ___ when the room is dark and quiet.
l1_interference: Falantes de português podem dizer 'sleep good' por confundir o advérbio 'bem' com o adjetivo 'bom'. Em inglês, depois do verbo usamos o advérbio: 'sleep well'.
explanation: In English, verbs of action are modified by adverbs, not adjectives. 'Well' is the adverb that goes with 'sleep' when we talk about the quality of sleep.

related_collocations.example: I get up early every morning to go to school.
She works hard before her exams.

memory_tip: WELL = adverb after verbs (sleep well, eat well) | GOOD = adjective before nouns (a good night)
